I am 70 years old, and I have farmed my 8 mu of irrigated land here in Quzhou County for most of my life. Because I have a high education level, I read the county agricultural bulletins and keep my own notebooks on yields and inputs. I do not chase risky new crops at my age; I stick to the wheat–maize double-cropping system that this North China Plain soil and climate were made for. My winter wheat was sown last October with an improved semi-dwarf variety, and now that it is reviving in April I am busy with the first spring irrigation and top-dressing with urea. After the wheat harvest in early June I will immediately plant a hybrid maize variety using no-tillage to save moisture and labour. I apply compound fertilizer as a basal dose and top-dress according to the crop stage. For wheat I rotary-till before sowing, irrigate four times (including the winter irrigation and two spring irrigations), and spray pesticides three times to control aphids, fusarium head blight, and weeds. For summer maize I use no-tillage, irrigate twice (at jointing and filling), and spray three times for corn borers and herbicides. I expect about 1,100 jin per mu from the wheat and about 1,200 jin per mu from the maize this year if the weather holds.
